chain_trace.break_detail: The DEFECT_FOUND verdict was declared on an extra-contractual oracle expectation. The contract->doc link promises 200 with one ordered result per search (satisfied by the raw response); neither the contract nor the versioned spec promises that a by-id query returns the referenced point itself. Source forensics shows the empty entry is the designed by-id semantics: the referenced id is resolved to its stored vector and then EXCLUDED from the search results via a must_not has_id filter (lib/collection/src/operations/universal_query/collection_query.rs:704-708 + 525-535, explicit code comments), so a by-id query over a single-point collection necessarily yields points:[]. The upsert-idempotence, overwrite-flip, stale-read, and count-invariance phenomena the attack actually targeted all PASSED (count==1 all waves; GET readback V1->V2 flip landed; point 500 visible to the same batch face via the vector query). The misalignment originates in the script oracle (docstring) and surfaces at the log verdict.
